Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Houston/Galveston TX
1202 AM CDT Fri Jul 31 2026

...New DISCUSSION, MARINE...

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Hot and dry today.

- A cold front will bring a chance for a few showers and
  thunderstorms Saturday afternoon/evening through very early
  Sunday. 
 
- Next week's outlook features seasonably hot and humid conditions
  with isolated afternoon showers and storms possible.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1200 AM CDT Fri Jul 31 2026

Texas remains in the grip of a strong mid/upper ridge centered over 
New Mexico. However, one can see signs of flux in the pattern by 
taking a gander at the water vapor imagery. Over the northern 
plains, there is a robust mid/upper disturbances that is trending 
from a strong shortwave trough to a more longer wave system. As 
ridging retrogrades into W CONUS this weekend, the aforementioned 
trough should help shift lower mid/upper heights westward in the 
central CONUS, eroding the ridge over Texas. The mid/upper system 
will also foment LL cyclogenesis, resulting in a sfc low that tracks 
across the Midwest this weekend. The low will have a trailing cold 
front that pushes into southeast Texas by Saturday afternoon or 
night. What do all these factors entail for our weather here in SE 
TX? 

The dry and hot regime will continue today. Inland afternoon highs 
in the upper 90s will be common once again, with a few areas 
reaching 100 degrees. Sufficient mixing should keep peak heating dew 
points low enough to prevent widespread heat indices reaching or 
exceeding 108F (Heat Advisory criteria). That being said, various 
locations did briefly reaching 108-109F on Thursday, so I suspect 
that will happen again today. Remember that normal Texas heat is 
dangerous. Today's temperatures should be a tad hotter than normal. 

The trailing cold front approaches the region on Saturday. The exact 
timing of the front will be crucial regarding convection and 
temperatures. LL frontal convergence may already be sufficient to 
initiate at least shallow convection along and ahead of the front. 
But moisture / thermodynamic profiles could allow for deep 
convection, especially if these forcings are able to interact with 
peak daytime heating. A front that waits until Saturday evening / 
night will have less day time heating to play with, while a Saturday 
afternoon FROPA will obviously have more. Couldn't rule out an 
isolated stronger thunderstorm if the timing works out. Saturday's 
temperatures are expected to be in the mid/upper 90s. But with a 
veering LL wind profile and enough sunshine ahead of the front, I 
couldn't rule out temperatures trying to spike up to around 100 
degrees in our central and southern counties ahead of the front. 

Interestingly, guidance has trended towards a somewhat stronger 
front, featuring much lower dew points in its wake. How far south 
this dry air extends is uncertain. But it appears dew points as low 
as the 50s could make it into our northern zones, while dew points 
well down into the 60s could push all the way to I-10. If the 
front's associated showers/storms/clouds are able to clear, yielding 
a bright, sunny Sunday with low dew points and light northerly flow, 
then it's possible my mid/upper 90s temps on Sunday are a little 
low. But I'll stick with mid/upper 90s for now. 

The outlook for next week continues to look seasonably miserable, 
with highs in the mid/upper 90s, isolated diurnal showers/storms, 
and heat indices well over 100 degrees. 


Self 


&&

.AVIATION...
(00Z TAF Issuance)
Issued at 651 PM CDT Thu Jul 30 2026

High pressure continues to bring VFR conditions with S-SW wind 
throughout the period. Winds become light and variable overnight but 
strengthen throughout the day on Friday with potential for 15-20kt 
gusts in the afternoon. MVFR CIGs are possible in the early morning 
as we saw today at our northern terminals but would burn off by late 
morning. An isolated SHRA with the afternoon sea breeze could occur 
but confidence is too low to include it in the current TAFs.

BSM

&&

.MARINE...
Issued at 1145 PM CDT Thu Jul 30 2026

Light to moderate SW winds should continue through Friday and into
Saturday. By Saturday afternoon and evening, SW winds are expected
to increase somewhat, possibly reaching up to 20 knots sustained
at times. This may result in a modest increase in seas. The 
chance of showers and thunderstorms increases late Saturday 
afternoon and evening as well. By Sunday into Monday, winds may
become westerly. Light to moderate S to SW winds return for
Tuesday and Wednesday.

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Lake Charles LA
1244 AM CDT Fri Jul 31 2026

...New DISCUSSION, AVIATION, MARINE, FIRE WEATHER...

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Dangerous heat continues through Saturday with afternoon highs in 
the mid to upper 90s and maximum heat indices of 102-109F.

- A weak frontal boundary will move through the region Saturday 
night into Sunday bringing a 30-70% chance of rain. Some slightly 
drier air may work into the region Sunday, but both high and low 
temperatures will remain largely unchanged. 

- A few, diurnally driven, afternoon thunderstorms are expected to
  develop each day next week. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
(Today through Thursday)
Issued at 1241 AM CDT Fri Jul 31 2026

Maximum heat index values Thursday afternoon ranged 
from 100-109. This justified the heat advisory although the majority 
of locations remained below the threshold. With afternoon highs and 
dewpoints expected to be very similar this afternoon, a repeat of 
max heat indices in that range is expected with the majority of the 
region remaining just below heat advisory criteria. 

The broad upper level ridge, part of the synoptic scale "omega" 
block pattern is expected to retrograde west into central and west 
Texas Friday night into Saturday morning as a somewhat unseasonable 
upper trough digs south through the central conus with guidance 
becoming more consistent in a weak frontal boundary making it all 
the way to the coast. Being the first week of August, it would be 
too much to ask for any cooler air to make it this far south. 
However, the boundary will develop some cloud cover along with some 
showers and thunderstorms as it moves through late Saturday night 
into Sunday morning. QPF totals are not very impressive, but it will 
be the first appreciable chance of precip the area has seen in over 
a week. 

It does look like the area will see a northwesterly wind shift 
behind the front Sunday which may drop dewpoints into the lower 70s 
or possibly even some upper 60s which is about as good as it gets in 
this part of the world in August. This won't translate into any 
actual change in temperatures, but the air may feel a bit less 
oppressively hot Sunday afternoon. Any reprieve will be short lived 
as the front washes out over the northern gulf Monday with winds 
turning back out of the south. 

The region will spend much of next week on the eastern periphery of 
the sprawling upper level ridge that will remain entrenched across 
the southwestern conus. This is expected to allow a few, diurnally 
driven storms, to develop each afternoon although the coverage will 
likely be lower than typical owing to the proximity of the ridge as 
well as limited moisture aloft. Afternoon highs will continue to 
range in the low to mid 90s each day.

Jones

&&

.AVIATION...
(06Z TAFS)
Issued at 1241 AM CDT Fri Jul 31 2026

High pressure over the northeastern gulf and ridging 
aloft will maintain VFR conditions through the taf period along with 
light south southwesterly winds.

Jones 

&&

.MARINE...
Issued at 1241 AM CDT Fri Jul 31 2026

Light southwesterly winds and low seas will continue 
through Saturday. A weak boundary will move through the coastal 
waters early Sunday which will increase west northwesterly winds to 
15-20 knots. The boundary will also increase thunderstorm chances. 
Light southerly flow becomes reestablished Monday through the rest 
of the week.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 1241 AM CDT Fri Jul 31 2026

Hot and humid conditions will continue through 
Saturday. Rain chances will increase Saturday night into Sunday as 
an upper level trough and weak frontal boundary approach the area. A 
brief period of northwesterly winds are expected Sunday bringing 
some slightly drier air into the region. Minimum RH's Sunday 
afternoon are expected to be in the 35-50% range. Winds will turn 
back out of the south Sunday night into Monday. Scattered afternoon 
thunderstorms will develop each day next week.
